item.title: South Korea To Prosecute Students Cheating With Smart Glasses
item.description: South Korea will file criminal complaints against students caught cheating on a national university entrance exam with smart glasses and toughen penalties for their use, a government official told AFP Friday. Sales of smart glasses — which allow the wearer to shoot photos and videos, and interact with an AI assistant among other abilities — are growing worldwide. But so is a backlash around the gadgets, including concerns over people being filmed without consent and their use by exam cheats. South Korea’s notoriously gruelling college entry exam, known as the “Suneung”, is essential for admission to top universities and widely regarded as a gateway to economic security and even a good marriage. “The ministry will seek criminal charges against students caught cheating with smart glasses” in the future, Lee Joon-hyuk, an education ministry official, told AFP. An optometrist holds a pair of smart glasses at the Eyedaq eyewear store in Seoul on October 30, 2026. Photo by JUNG YEON-JE / AFP Under authorities’ plans, students caught cheating with smart glasses will not be able to retake their exams for three years, an extension from the current penalty of one year. But the new rules are unlikely to apply to next month’s college entrance tests, Lee said. “With only about 20 days left until the exam, it would be realistically difficult to amend the law before then. However, we plan to push for the changes to take effect from next year’s exam,” he said. It comes after three students were caught wearing or possessing smart glasses during institution-administered essay exams at universities in Seoul. Their use is an emerging issue at schools worldwide. This summer, the prestigious National Taiwan University in Taipei reportedly disqualified an entrance exam candidate for cheating using AI smart glasses. A pair of smart glasses is pictured on display at the Eyedaq eyewear store in Seoul on October 30, 2026. Photo by JUNG YEON-JE / AFP Seoul’s education ministry’s new measures to prevent cheating using smart glasses, announced Thursday, included assigning a “designated staff member” at each examination centre to identify suspicious eyewear. With so much at stake, on the day of the Suneung, a 35-minute nationwide ban on flights is imposed during the English listening test, except in emergencies, while banks and public offices tell their workers to start an hour later to avoid traffic on the roads. Enormous pressure placed on students in South Korea’s ultra-competitive education system has been partly blamed for teenage depression and suicide rates that are among the highest in the world. item.title: Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than $2.5bn frozen
item.description: Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Thursday it had fallen victim to a major hack that had resulted in the freezing of more than $2.5 billion in an effort to prevent them from being stolen. The company — the world’s largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes — said it had suspended trading on certain products. It nevertheless insisted: “User funds are completely safe.” Several experts said it looked like a massive amount of assets had been stolen. “It does look like a hack on Binance,” said former Binance chief Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the group but remains a majority shareholder. Paolo Ardoino, the CEO of Tether — a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT — said his firm froze about $1.6 billion “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.” Circle boss Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC. USDT and USDC are both “stablecoins,” or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar. For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, several industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform. Some said it could be the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind, with a haul exceeding the $1.5 billion stolen in February 2025 from the Bybit platform — an incident attributed to hackers affiliated with North Korea. item.title: AFCON to hold every two years again as CAF reverses decision
item.description: The Confederation of African Football (CAF) has reversed its decision to stage the Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) every four years, announcing that the tournament will return to its traditional two-year cycle. The decision was unanimously approved by the CAF Executive Committee, with President Patrice Motsepe announcing the development after the organisation’s Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde, held from October 7 to 9, 2026. The reversal comes after CAF reviewed its earlier plan to move AFCON to a four-year schedule and introduce an Africa Nations League as a biennial competition. CAF said the proposed Nations League would take several years to generate the financial resources and football development benefits required to make its competitions globally competitive and financially sustainable. In a statement published on its website on Thursday, Motsepe said the decision to retain the two-year AFCON cycle was taken in the interest of African football, the confederation’s 54 member associations and African players playing for clubs outside the continent. “The decision by the CAF EXCO that the CAF AFCON should take place every Two Years was based on advancing, protecting and promoting the interest of African Football and CAF’s 54 Member Associations, as well as the interest of African players employed by Football Clubs outside Africa,” he said. Motsepe added that CAF was concerned about the time it would take for the proposed Africa Nations League to deliver the financial and developmental gains initially expected from the competition. He said the new tournament was intended to mirror the existing AFCON format and take place every two years, but would not provide the required support for African football in the immediate future. Under the revised calendar, the next AFCON will take place in 2027, with Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda jointly hosting the tournament. The subsequent editions are scheduled for 2028, 2031 and 2033, with CAF maintaining that the competition will not be staged in a FIFA World Cup year. Motsepe expressed confidence in the three East African countries’ ability to deliver a successful tournament in 2027. He also described AFCON as more than a football competition, saying it provides an opportunity to celebrate Africa’s cultures and bring people from across the continent and the diaspora together. “The AFCON competition is also about celebrating African Football and Africa’s rich and diverse cultures, customs and traditions and bringing people together from Africa’s 54 Countries, the African Diaspora and throughout the world,” he said. “The CAF EXCO decision is in the best interest of African Football and CAF’s 54 Member Associations and will also contribute significantly to the development and growth of football in Africa,” he added. item.title: Gunmen kill four in Plateau community
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Four persons were reportedly killed when gunmen attacked Sabon Angwa community, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area of Plateau State, on Thursday night. The attackers were said to have stormed the community at about 8pm and opened fire on residents, despite the curfew imposed in parts of the state to check attacks and restore security. A resident of Barkin Ladi, Mr Bulus Jok, who confirmed the incident, said, “The gunmen struck the community around 8pm despite the curfew in place and started shooting sporadically.” Jok said, “They were shooting at anything they saw. The attack created panic in the community, and four people were killed.” He added, “The incident is very sad, especially as there had been an early warning alert sent to the relevant authorities a day before the attack.” Also confirming the incident, Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, BYM, Mr Rwang Tengwong, said, “Terrorist gangs reportedly attacked Sabon Angwa, around Bet/Zat in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area, and shot four people dead.” Tengwong condemned the attack, describing the killing of innocent residents as unacceptable, adding, “We condemn this latest attack in strong terms and lament the loss of these lives.” He said, “It is disturbing that communities are still being attacked despite the security measures and curfew put in place to protect residents.” The BYM spokesman urged security operatives to intensify surveillance and take proactive measures to prevent further attacks on vulnerable communities, saying, “We call on security agencies to strengthen their presence and respond promptly to early warning alerts.” Efforts to reach security operatives for more details were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, October 30, 2026
item.description: The Nigerian Naira opened today, Friday, October 30, 2026, holding firm against the United States Dollar across both the official foreign exchange window and the parallel market, following sustained liquidity interventions by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) and healthy diaspora inflows. At the official Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), the spot exchange rate traded at N1,346.86 per dollar during early morning transactions. Commercial banks and corporate importers observed orderly liquidity conditions as FX demand for trade obligations, tuition fees, and capital repatriation continued to be met across authorized channels. In the parallel market, commonly referred to as the black market, street traders and Bureau De Change operators across major economic centers, including Lagos, Abuja, and Kano, quoted buying rates around N1,375 per dollar, while selling rates hovered around N1,385 per dollar. The price gap between the official market and the parallel window remains narrow. Financial analysts attribute the relative stability of the local currency to Nigeria’s solid foreign reserve buffer, which remains well above $55 billion, enabling the central bank to cushion short-term demand shocks and maintain stability across trading channels. Market experts expect trading to remain steady throughout the business day as routine demand is steadily absorbed by market liquidity. item.title: PSC promotes 2 DIGs, 10 AIGs, 17 CPs, 3,800 others
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the promotion of more than 3,800 senior police officers, including two Deputy Inspectors-General of Police (DIGs), 10 Assistant Inspectors-General of Police (AIGs) and 17 Commissioners of Police (CPs). The promotions followed the officers’ successful participation in promotion examinations and oral interviews conducted by the commission. A statement issued by the PSC on Thursday said the approvals were granted at its plenary meeting in Abuja, presided over by its Chairman, DIG Hashimu Salihu Argungu (rtd). The two officers elevated to the rank of DIG are AIG Olaolu Adegbite, Head of INTERPOL National Central Bureau, Abuja, and AIG Dankombo F. Morris, who heads Zone 4 Headquarters, Makurdi. Adegbite holds a BA in Russian Language from the University of Lagos and an MA in Philology from the Pushkin Institute, Moscow. He is a recipient of the national honour of Member of the Order of the Federal Republic (MFR), a member of the FBI National Academy Associates and an alumnus of Harvard Kennedy School. He previously served as Director of Operations at the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). Morris, who hails from Gombe State, holds a BA in History from the University of Maiduguri and a Diploma in Police Science. He has served as Commissioner of Police in Adamawa State. item.title: NESG: Nigeria’s high production costs threaten industrial competitiveness
item.description: By Favour Ulebor The Nigeria Economic Summit Group has warned that high production costs, unreliable electricity and poor logistics infrastructure are undermining Nigeria’s industrial competitiveness, calling for a council within the Presidency to coordinate industrialisation policies. Co-facilitator of the NESG, Lumun Feese, said Nigeria needed a coordinated approach to industrial development to address structural challenges and enable local manufacturers to compete effectively in African markets. She spoke at a breakout session on building an integrated industrial ecosystem during the 32nd Nigeria Economic Summit in Abuja. Feese said Nigeria had dropped from eighth to 14th position on the African Development Bank’s Africa Industrialisation Index, although she noted that the methodology had changed and more countries had been included in the latest ranking. She said, “We are not maximising our potential and our large economy. “How do we go and compete in South Africa when our cost of production is so high? Feese said the proposed industrialisation, competitiveness and regional integration council would provide a central coordinating platform within the Presidency to align government policies, improve implementation of the National Industrial Policy and strengthen private-sector participation. She said Nigerian businesses needed reliable power, efficient transportation systems and lower production costs to take advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area, which offers access to a wider continental market. Feese said the recommendations followed consultations on mining, the blue economy, power, oil and gas, and industrial competitiveness. She urged businesses and other stakeholders to sustain their engagement with the NESG’s Industrial Policy Commission, saying coordinated policies and consistent implementation were necessary to achieve measurable industrial growth. Other stakeholders at the session identified limited access to finance, skills shortages, regulatory bottlenecks, security concerns and inadequate export infrastructure as major obstacles to industrial growth. Special Assistant on Strategy to the Minister of State for Industry, Gerald Okunsebor, called for greater awareness of the National Industrial Policy and a clear implementation framework with defined responsibilities, timelines and accountability mechanisms. He said a central knowledge-management system was also needed to ensure continuity in industrial development policies across successive administrations. item.title: Nigeria’s export earnings rise 23.7% to $35.6bn in H1’26
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe Nigeria’s total export earnings rose by 23.7 per cent year-on-year, YoY to $35.64 billion in the first half of 2026 (H1’26), from $28.82 billion in the corresponding period of 2025, driven largely by a surge in petroleum products exports. Analysis of data from the quarterly statistical bulletin, of the Central Bank of Nigeria’s (CBN) for Q2’26, showed that the country’s export earnings increased by $6.82 billion during the six-month period, with petroleum products accounting for about 65 per cent of the growth. Petroleum products exports jumped by 238.7 per cent YoY to $6.31 billion in H1’26 from $1.86 billion in H1’25, representing an increase of approximately $4.45 billion. Crude oil remained Nigeria’s largest individual export category, generating $17.51 billion, up 7.7 per cent YoY from $16.25 billion in the corresponding period of 2025. Gas exports also increased, rising by 4.2 per cent YoY to $6.22 billion from $5.97 billion. Consequently, total exports of crude oil, gas and petroleum products rose by 21.9 per cent YoY to $30.03 billion from $24.63 billion in H1’25. The performance indicates that petroleum-related exports remained the dominant source of Nigeria’s export earnings, accounting for about 84.3 per cent of total exports during the period. Meanwhile, non-oil exports increased by 18.2 per cent YoY to $5.60 billion from $4.74 billion in H1’25. Despite the increase, non-oil exports accounted for about 15.7 per cent of total export earnings, down from approximately 16.5 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025. The commission, however, gave a window of 14 days to those omitted to forward their petitions to the commission for possible review. Our correspondents report that after the close of submission on the 24th, in which all the affected filed their petitions, INEC promised to come up with a final decision on the petitions on the 29th. And after a meeting which lasted for over six hours on Thursday, it declared that some of the candidates have been cleared. A competent source at INEC, who spoke to Daily Trust after the commission’s meeting on Thursday, said the commission received 69 petitions from political parties concerning omitted candidates for governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections. The source said about 36 petitions were successful, while the others failed. “We received a total of 69 petitions from political parties. Some of the successful ones, I think about 36, and the rest didn’t succeed,” the source said. The source, however, said the commission was still awaiting the final figures from its legal department. On Pantami and Gwarzo, the source said the commission had no objection to their candidacy, but noted that the pending court cases could affect their eligibility. “Yes, Pantami has been cleared,” the source said when asked about the PDP candidate in Gombe State. On Gwarzo, the source said his clearance remained subject to the outcome of the litigation involving his candidacy. “Because of the court case, the court may rule otherwise. So his approval is subject to whatever the court finally decides,” the source said. The official added that the commission had no issues with either candidate contesting the election. “We have no issues with them contesting as candidates,” the source said. On Adebutu’s, the source said, “He did not succeed.” The decisions followed complaints by candidates and political parties after INEC omitted their names from the lists published ahead of the 2027 general elections. Pantami and Gwarzo were among the prominent governorship candidates whose names were missing from the commission’s list released in October. INEC had attributed the omissions to alleged non-compliance by some political parties with provisions of the Electoral Act, 2026, requiring parties to submit their membership registers. The commission said its position followed a September 24, 2026, Supreme Court judgement affirming the constitutionality of Section 77(5) to (7) of the Electoral Act, which makes the submission of membership registers mandatory. Gwarzo had approached the court to challenge the omission of his name and that of his running mate, Rabiu Mustapha, from the list of governorship candidates for Kano State. In an originating summons dated October 20, 2026, he asked the court to declare their exclusion unlawful and compel INEC to recognise them as the NDC’s governorship candidates. Pantami’s candidacy has also been the subject of litigation, with the INEC source noting that a court proceeding was expected on Friday. Meanwhile, Adebutu had questioned his exclusion from the final list of governorship candidates in Ogun State, insisting that he remained a registered member of the PDP and had complied with the party’s membership registration requirements. Daily Trust gathered that INEC will issue a formal statement on the outcome of the review. It was not clear as at press time if the Kaduna NDC governorship candidate, Senator Danjuma Laah and the Social Democratic Party (SDP) governorship candidate for Benue State, Sebastine Hon had been cleared. Reacting to the restoration of the candidate’s name by INEC, Shuaibu said the party was never alarmed by the earlier development, saying it was convinced that all electoral requirements had been met. According to him, the decision came as no surprise, as party members viewed the omission as a temporary setback that would eventually be corrected. “We were not frightened because we followed all the laid-down procedures from party membership to the nomination process and submission of our candidate’s details,” he said. Shuaibu argued that the episode had generated public sympathy and attracted more supporters to the party. “What the electoral commission intended as a setback has actually worked in our favour. It has increased our supporters, strengthened our popularity and made more people identify with us,” he said. He added that the party would continue mobilising voters and promoting its programmes across the state, expressing confidence that the development had further boosted its chances in the forthcoming governorship election. item.title: Omitted candidates: INEC upholds 41 of governorship petitions, rejects 28
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has upheld 41 of the 69 petitions filed against the final list of governorship candidates for the 2027 general election, while rejecting 28. Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC) of the commission, Mohammed Kudu Haruna, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday night. According to him, the petitions came from 12 political parties across 26 states. item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi & Ben Ngwakwe There were strong indications on Thursday night that the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC might have provisionally cleared a former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy and Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Gombe State, Prof. Isa Ali Ibrahim Pantami, and the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Kano State, Abdulsalam Gwarzo, to contest the 2027 elections. The clearance of both men is subject to the outcome of pending court cases, it was learned on Thursday night. In Gombe, Pantami’s supporters took over some major areas celebrating the development on Thursday night. INEC officials did not immediately react to Vanguard’s questions regarding the development. But a source said the decisions were reached at the commission’s meeting on Thursday to consider complaints from political parties and candidates whose names were left out of the lists published ahead of the 2027 elections. The source added that the commission had no objection to their candidacies, but that the pending legal proceedings could still affect the final outcome. The development comes after INEC dropped Pantami’s name from the final list of governorship candidates for Gombe State, although he appeared on the provisional list published on August 29. Pantami emerged as the PDP candidate after leaving the All Progressives Congress (APC) on May 19. One of the aspirants for the ticket, Ahmed Mailantarki Mailantarki, challenged his victory in court. A Federal High Court sitting in Gombe nullified the election and ordered a fresh primary, which Pantami won again. His biggest hurdle was the September 24 Supreme Court judgement, which restored Sections 77(5), (6), (7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act 2026. The provisions bar parties from fielding candidates whose names were not in the membership register submitted to INEC within the stipulated time. Mohammed Haruna, an INEC National Commissioner, had previously said that, in line with the Supreme Court ruling, some parties would not field candidates in 2027. The commission, however, rejected a petition by the PDP governorship candidate in Ogun State, Ladi Adebutu, who had asked it to review his exclusion from the list of candidates. item.title: Taraba massacre: Reps seek urgent help as death toll hits 60
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina Abuja—The House of Representatives has called for urgent security and humanitarian intervention, following a deadly bandit attack on Binnari community in Karim Lamido Local Government Area of Taraba State, with the death toll reportedly reaching 60. Read Also: Armed bandits raid Taraba community, loot food stores The lawmakers also urged stronger security cooperation among Taraba, Plateau and Bauchi states to tackle the persistent attacks and prevent further loss of lives. The appeal followed a motion on the attack, which reportedly occurred on October 23, 2026, leaving dozens dead and residents displaced. The House called for immediate relief for affected residents and urged the relevant authorities to expedite the completion of the Wase–Karim Lamido road to improve access and security in the area. Contributing to the debate, Minority Leader, Fredrick Agbedi, criticised what he described as the overreliance on resolutions and minutes of silence in response to recurring security crises, insisting on practical measures to protect lives. He called for a technology-driven security response, stressing the need for improved intelligence gathering, surveillance and coordinated operations to confront the attackers. In his response, the Deputy Speaker cited government efforts to address insecurity, including the neutralisation of terrorists, surrenders by insurgents, a reduction in the number of local government areas under insurgent control and increased spending on security. The House’s intervention underscores growing concerns over the humanitarian consequences of repeated attacks in parts of the country and the need for coordinated action by federal and state authorities. The lawmakers urged the relevant agencies to act urgently to restore security, provide relief to victims and prevent further attacks on vulnerable communities. These symptoms can resemble malaria, typhoid and other common infections, making a patient’s travel history and possible exposure important parts of clinical assessment. Symptoms generally appear between two and 21 days after exposure. According to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), Ebola spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of infected people or deceased patients, infected animals, or contaminated materials. Early identification, laboratory confirmation, isolation, contact tracing and strict infection prevention and control measures are essential to containing outbreaks. Adesanya cautioned against the belief that every infected person must bleed visibly. “Contrary to popular belief, not every Ebola patient experiences bleeding. In fact, severe dehydration, shock and multiple organ failure are among the major causes of death.” “Vomiting and diarrhoea can cause substantial fluid and electrolyte loss, resulting in dehydration, falling blood pressure and shock. The disease can also damage the liver, kidneys and other organs.” Waiting for bleeding before suspecting “Ebola can therefore be dangerous. Patients may need urgent medical intervention before advanced symptoms appear, while exposed individuals may need to be identified and monitored. “Early diagnosis saves two lives. The life of the infected patient and potentially the lives of others who might otherwise become infected,” Adesanya said. The lesson from Adadevoh’s experience is not that every fever should be treated as Ebola, but that clinicians must consider relevant exposure risks and promptly assess suspected cases through appropriate medical and public health channels. Why Ebola outbreaks keep returning Containing an outbreak does not mean the virus has been eradicated. Ebola is a zoonotic disease, meaning it can pass from animals to humans. As long as Ebola viruses continue circulating in their natural environment, further spillover into human populations remains possible. According to Adesanya, certain fruit bats are considered likely natural reservoirs for some Ebola viruses, although their ecology and the precise pathways of transmission are not fully understood. Human infection may occur through contact with infected wildlife or their bodily fluids. Once the virus enters the human population, it can spread through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of infected people, including deceased patients, or through contaminated materials. In an interview with Vanguard, Adesanya identified several factors that make outbreaks difficult to prevent. Surveillance systems may be weak in remote communities where healthcare and laboratory services are limited. Conflict and population displacement can disrupt health services, while poverty can prevent people from accessing treatment centres. Distrust of authorities may also discourage communities from reporting suspected cases or cooperating with public health teams. Adesanya said Ebola viruses may persist in certain body fluids of survivors after recovery, occasionally resulting in renewed transmission. International travel and migration add another challenge because an infected person may cross national borders before the infection is detected. “Therefore, Ebola cannot be controlled through hospital treatment alone. It requires a comprehensive One Health approach, integrating human health, animal health and environmental surveillance. “The approach recognises that human health is connected to animal health and the environment. Treatment remains a challenge Ebola is not automatically a death sentence. Survival depends on the virus species, the patient’s condition and how quickly appropriate care begins. According to Adesanya, no approved virus-specific treatment or vaccine is currently available for Bundibugyo virus disease. Effective care requires functional treatment and isolation facilities, diagnostic laboratories, reliable supplies and trained healthcare workers. Healthcare workers must also have the protective equipment and safe working conditions needed to prevent infection. In a statement titled “From Reforms to Delivery: Our Infrastructure Investment and Growth Strategy,” Tinubu said the focus should be on the economic value generated by borrowed funds rather than the amount borrowed. “The real question is not how much we borrow, but what we build, what value we create and what future we leave behind,” he said. The President identified the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, Sokoto-Badagry Superhighway, Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity grid upgrades and modernisation of key commercial ports in Lagos as major projects expected to strengthen Nigeria’s productive capacity. He said investments in healthcare, education and vocational training will complement the infrastructure projects by connecting economic regions, reducing logistics costs, unlocking agricultural and industrial potential and attracting private investment. According to him, the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is expected to reduce logistics costs along its corridor by 15 to 20 per cent and potentially add up to two per cent to Nigeria’s Gross Domestic Product, GDP, through increased trade, tourism and industrial activity. The project is also projected to generate about 100,000 direct jobs in construction and engineering, alongside more than 150,000 indirect jobs in logistics, materials and related services. Tinubu said: “We are not simply building highways, we are opening economic corridors, connecting markets, unlocking industries and reshaping Nigeria’s economic geography.” He argued that achieving his administration’s ambition of building a $1 trillion economy by 2030 will require sustained investment in infrastructure to support productivity, industrialisation and trade. “We cannot build a $1 trillion economy with infrastructure designed for an economy a fraction of that size,” he said. Cites economic indicators The President said reforms introduced since May 2023 had helped restore macro-economic stability, strengthen public finances and improve Nigeria’s standing in international financial markets. He cited real GDP growth of 4.43 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 and a decline in headline inflation to 14.63 per cent in September from 20.98 per cent a year earlier. He added that gross external reserves rose to $55.1 billion as of October 9, 2026, including about $46 billion in net reserves, while the tax-to-GDP ratio increased to 12.5 per cent from seven per cent. Tinubu attributed the reported improvements to measures including petrol subsidy removal, exchange rate unification, tax reforms and coordinated efforts to tackle inflation. “The decisions taken since 2023 were difficult but necessary,” he said. According to him, the reforms had strengthened Nigeria’s capacity to attract investment and finance projects that support long-term economic growth. “Confidence has a price; our cost of borrowing is going down, and the country risk premium has drastically decreased,” he said. The President cited positive assessments by international credit rating agencies as evidence of improving investor confidence. “These are not political endorsements, they are independent assessments by global rating agencies, index providers, regulators and investors, recognising stronger external reserves, improved macroeconomic management and greater financial credibility,” he said. He argued that the improved standing could help Nigeria attract institutional investors, secure longer-term financing and reduce borrowing costs. Tinubu said the government was shifting public borrowing away from financing short-term fiscal pressures towards investments expected to generate economic returns, create jobs and expand opportunities for future generations. He added that longer-term financing arrangements would help match repayment periods with the lifespan of infrastructure assets, reduce refinancing pressures and secure more competitive funding for productive investments. Lists economic priorities The President said Nigeria must convert renewed international confidence into capital expenditure, completed infrastructure and lasting benefits for citizens. He outlined five priorities for the next phase of the Federal Executive Council’s economic strategy: food affordability and energy price stability; budget harmonisation and fiscal discipline; completion of high-impact projects and investment in critical infrastructure; an improved economic policy framework and regulatory efficiency; and targeted household support alongside investment in human development. He said the administration’s economic performance would ultimately be measured by completed projects, increased investment, job creation and improved living standards. “Securing financing is not the achievement. Completing the project, delivering value and improving the lives of Nigerians is the achievement,” he said. The President added that Nigeria’s economic ambitions must be backed by responsible borrowing and investments that create lasting opportunities for future generations. NLC faults fresh external loans However, NLC President, Mr. Joe Ajaero, questioned the justification for the proposed loans, particularly against the backdrop of the Federal Government’s claims of increased revenue following the removal of petrol subsidy. Speaking on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief yesterday, Ajaero challenged the government to explain why it continued to seek loans from international financial institutions despite the reported increase in revenue. “If you come out to tell us that subsidy is gone, that you are making more money and then you are giving more money to states, what is the justification for continually borrowing from the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank and other agencies when there is enough money?” he asked. The labour leader argued that continued borrowing is worsening the country’s debt burden and questioned whether loans from international financial institutions necessarily served Nigeria’s best interests. He also cited rising crude oil prices, which he attributed to tensions in the Middle East, as another reason government should reconsider its borrowing plans. “If the 2026 budget was prepared with crude oil price benchmarked at $70 per barrel and now sells above $100 per barrel due to the US-Iran crisis, should this country still be taking loans?” Ajaero asked. He argued that increased oil earnings and revenue accruing to oil-producing states should prompt the Federal Government to explain why additional external borrowing remained necessary. Ajaero, however, clarified that the NLC has no authority to approve or reject government loans, noting that such decisions rested with the relevant government institutions. He urged Nigerians and relevant agencies to demand greater accountability from the Federal Government over its borrowing plans. item.description: By Ishola Balogun The Mosque Guidance and Development Lagos Initiative (MGDLI) has called on Muslims across Lagos State to actively participate in its forthcoming three-day anniversary programme, describing the event as a unique opportunity to contribute to the development of stronger mosques and a more vibrant Muslim community. The organisation extended the invitation to Imams, mosque administrators, Islamic scholars, youth groups, Muslim professionals, community leaders and all members of the Ummah to attend and benefit from the activities lined up for the anniversary celebration. The programme, scheduled for October 30 to November 1, 2026, will be held at the Lagos State First Secretariat Mosque Hall (Olanike Hall), Shamsi Adisa Thomas Central Mosque, Ikeja GRA, Lagos. MGDLI said broad participation by Muslims is essential to achieving the collective goal of building mosques that are better managed, cleaner, safer and more responsive to the needs of worshippers and their communities. “The responsibility of developing our mosques does not rest solely on Imams and mosque committees. Every Muslim has a role to play in building institutions that reflect the values of Islam, accountability, cleanliness and service to humanity,” the organisation stated. The anniversary programme will feature special prayers during the Jumu’ah service, health outreach activities, sanitation and hygiene training, first-aid sensitisation, a keynote lecture and networking sessions. According to MGDLI, the event presents an opportunity for members of the Ummah to gain valuable knowledge, exchange ideas and support efforts aimed at improving mosque administration and community welfare. The organisation said the programme aligns with Islamic teachings that promote cleanliness, good governance, communal responsibility and mutual support. “This gathering is not merely an anniversary celebration; it is a call to action for Muslims to work collectively towards building stronger institutions and healthier communities,” MGDLI said. The initiative also appealed to philanthropists, Islamic organisations, corporate bodies and community stakeholders to support the programme and partner in future mosque development projects. Participants will also benefit from a medical outreach organised in collaboration with Lagos State University Teaching Hospital Muslim Nurse Forum, offering free health checks, blood pressure and blood sugar screening, counselling and referrals. “We invite every member of the Ummah to be part of this transformative programme. The organisation extended the invitation to Imams, mosque administrators, Islamic scholars, youth groups, Muslim professionals, community leaders and all members of the Ummah to attend and benefit from the activities lined up for the anniversary celebration. The programme, scheduled for October 30 to November 1, 2026, will be held at the Lagos State First Secretariat Mosque Hall (Olanike Hall), Shamsi Adisa Thomas Central Mosque, Ikeja GRA, Lagos. MGDLI said broad participation by Muslims is essential to achieving the collective goal of building mosques that are better managed, cleaner, safer and more responsive to the needs of worshippers and their communities. “The responsibility of developing our mosques does not rest solely on Imams and mosque committees. Every Muslim has a role to play in building institutions that reflect the values of Islam, accountability, cleanliness and service to humanity,” the organisation stated. The anniversary programme will feature special prayers during the Jumu’ah service, health outreach activities, sanitation and hygiene training, first-aid sensitisation, a keynote lecture and networking sessions. According to MGDLI, the event presents an opportunity for members of the Ummah to gain valuable knowledge, exchange ideas and support efforts aimed at improving mosque administration and community welfare. The organisation said the programme aligns with Islamic teachings that promote cleanliness, good governance, communal responsibility and mutual support. “This gathering is not merely an anniversary celebration; it is a call to action for Muslims to work collectively towards building stronger institutions and healthier communities,” MGDLI said. The initiative also appealed to philanthropists, Islamic organisations, corporate bodies and community stakeholders to support the programme and partner in future mosque development projects. Participants will also benefit from a medical outreach organised in collaboration with Lagos State University Teaching Hospital Muslim Nurse Forum, offering free health checks, blood pressure and blood sugar screening, counselling and referrals. “We invite every member of the Ummah to be part of this transformative programme. Together, we can build better and cleaner mosques, we can build stronger communities and a brighter future for coming generations,” MGDLI added. As both tracks accelerate, the risk grows that one will undermine the other. On 21 October 2026, the House of Representatives Ad Hoc Committee investigating poor telecom service quality gave the chief executives of MTN Nigeria, Airtel Nigeria, Globacom and Mafab Communications seven days to appear before it, and warned that those who refused would face arrest warrants. The committee chairman, Rep. Olumide Osoba (APC-Ogun), framed the matter in economic terms, noting that mobile connectivity now underpins point-of-sale operations, financial transactions and everyday commerce. Osoba alleged that invited CEOs repeatedly sent lower-ranking staff instead of appearing in person, calling the pattern unacceptable. This was not the first salvo. In May 2026, the House had already faulted the NCC for what lawmakers described as weak regulatory oversight, accusing the commission of failing to enforce standards that would compel operators to deliver reliable service. Rep. George Ozodinobi, the deputy minority whip, accused operators of prioritising profits over quality. The chamber then directed the NCC to tighten its quality-of-service standards and constituted the ad hoc committee to investigate the root causes of poor service. The NCC Has Been Proactive Meanwhile, the NCC has been building. In March 2026, the commission issued a landmark directive mandating mobile operators to compensate subscribers automatically when network performance falls below prescribed thresholds. The Framework for Compensation of Consumers, which took effect in April 2026, represents a fundamental shift in Nigeria’s telecom regulatory approach: for the first time, the burden of proving and pursuing redress moved from the subscriber to the operator. By October, NCC Executive Vice Chairman Dr Aminu Maida reported at the 95th Telecom Consumer Parliament in Lagos that more than 75 million subscribers had received airtime or data compensation for service failures recorded between November 2025 and September 2026. Nearly three million subscribers also received refunds for failed airtime and data transactions, while operators carried out more than 6,500 network interventions in the same period. Maida, however, struck a careful tone about the framework’s limits, cautioning that compensation alone falls short of solving the underlying problem. He noted that while redress matters, it cannot recover a lost business opportunity or a conversation that could not take place. His stated priority remains reducing the failures that make compensation necessary. The framework has also drawn praise from the industry. The National Consumers Advocacy Network commended the NCC for introducing automatic compensation without requiring subscribers to file complaints, calling the approach a new benchmark for regulatory innovation. Legal analysts at Tope Adebayo LP described the model as a significant consumer protection intervention, though they noted critical gaps, particularly the absence of any right of appeal for subscribers who consider the compensation inadequate. The Risk of Political Overreach Legislative oversight of critical sectors is legitimate and necessary. But holding regulators accountable differs from short-circuiting the very mechanisms those regulators are building. The NCC’s compensation framework is still in its first year of operation. The commission independently verifies operators’ claims of compliance. The Quality of Service Business Rules 2024, which underpin the framework, are being enforced alongside a broader programme of non-monetary sanctions. This is precisely the kind of technocratic, data-driven enforcement that Nigeria’s telecom sector has needed for years. The risk is that aggressive parliamentary intervention (arrest threats, public hearings designed for television rather than resolution, blanket accusations of extortion) sends operators into a defensive posture rather than a compliance posture. Telecoms CEOs, compelled to spend time answering lawmakers, have less time to invest in the infrastructure upgrades the country desperately needs. Mobile operators and tower companies invested a combined N2.5 trillion in network infrastructure in 2025 alone, yet service complaints persist, largely because Nigeria’s explosive urban growth and chronic infrastructure vandalism outpace even substantial capital deployment. Moreover, when the legislature openly questions the NCC’s competence while the commission is still rolling out a framework the House itself called for, the signal to the market is confusion, not accountability. As Tope Adebayo LP’s analysis of the framework observed, automatic compensation is only as effective as the data, transparency and enforcement discipline behind it. Undermining the regulator’s credibility while its enforcement machinery is running risks rendering the framework a dead letter and resolving nothing for the millions of subscribers the House claims to represent. What the Sector Needs Nigeria’s telecom subscribers deserve better service. On this, there is no disagreement between the House of Representatives, the NCC, and the industry itself. The question is whether the tools being deployed complement or contradict each other. The compensation framework, for all its early-stage limitations, is a structural answer to a structural problem. It creates automatic financial consequences for service failure, removes the procedural burden from subscribers, and aligns Nigeria’s regulatory approach with global best practice. It deserves space to mature, be tested, and be refined, not be trampled by parliamentary grandstanding that produces headlines but no new base stations. What would help is a legislature that reinforces the NCC’s enforcement authority rather than undermining it; that holds the commission accountable for the pace and rigour of its verification exercises rather than bypassing the regulator entirely; and that addresses the infrastructure vandalism, right-of-way obstacles and power supply crises that operators consistently cite as the root causes of service failure. The House has the right to investigate. The question is whether it will exercise that right in a way that strengthens the regulatory architecture, or tears it apart in search of a soundbite. item.title: Court sacks Uzodinma as APC senatorial candidate for Imo West
item.description: …orders INEC to recognise ex-Gov Okorocha By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja The Federal High Court in Abuja on Thursday nullified the emergence of Governor Hope Uzodinma as candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the Imo West Senatorial election slated for January 16, 2027. The court, in a judgment delivered by Justice Obiora Egwuatu, held that evidence before it established that Governor Uzodinma was not the valid winner of the primary election the APC conducted in the senatorial zone on May 18, which was monitored by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). According to the court, it was a former governor of the state, Senator Rochas Okorocha, who garnered the highest number of votes cast at the primary election and therefore ought to have been nominated by the party. Consequently, Justice Egwuatu ordered INEC to forthwith recognise Senator Okorocha and publish his name as the authentic candidate of the APC for the senatorial poll. It further issued an order barring Governor Uzodinma from presenting himself as the candidate of the APC for the election. item.title: [VIDEO] Umrah: Tinubu Arrives In Saudi Arabia
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has arrived in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The President landed at the King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, on Thursday night. ﻿ He was received by the Nigerian ambassador to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, Yakubu Gambo, and Saudi’s head of Royal Protocol, Ahmad bin Thafir. Tinubu is in the country to perform Umrah, an Islamic spiritual exercise involving a pilgrimage to the Holy City. He departed Abuja for Makkah on Thursday afternoon. The event is an opportunity for spiritual reflection, devotion, and prayers for the nation’s peace, unity, stability, and continued progress, Tinubu’s media aide, Bayo Onanuga, said in a statement on Wednesday. According to the statement, the President will perform the religious rites associated with Umrah, seeking Allah’s guidance and blessings for Nigeria and its people. He is expected back in the country next week. The post [VIDEO] Umrah: Tinubu Arrives In Saudi Arabia appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: ‘X-Men,’ ‘Star Trek’ Star Patrick Stewart Dies At 86
item.description: Patrick Stewart, the British Shakespearean actor who became a Hollywood megastar through roles in the “Star Trek” and “X-Men” franchises, has died at the age of 86, an official statement said Thursday. “We announce with great sorrow the passing of Sir Patrick Stewart yesterday at his home in Los Angeles, in the loving care of his beloved wife Sunny, following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” the statement said. The actor, who hailed from the northern English region of Yorkshire, trod the boards in Britain with the Royal Shakespeare Company before crossing the Atlantic to enjoy an acclaimed career on the US stage and screen. His best known Hollywood roles were as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in “Star Trek: The Next Generation” and Professor Charles Xavier in multiple “X-Men” and related Marvel films. British actor Sir Patrick Stewart arrives to Paramount+ Star Trek Day held at Skirball Cultural Center in Los Angeles, California, on September 8, 2022. Photo by MICHAEL TRAN / AFP “His sonorous voice and singular talent will forever be synonymous with indelible performances in every genre,” the statement said. “He explored the human condition in all its poetic complexity and brought hope not only to the far reaches of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, but into science fiction’s most iconic final frontier aboard the Starship Enterprise.” AFP The post ‘X-Men,’ ‘Star Trek’ Star Patrick Stewart Dies At 86 appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 2027: Tinubu Can Be Sure Of Victory In Imo With My Name On Ballot — Okorocha
item.description: Former Imo State Governor Rochas Okorocha has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will win Imo State in the 2027 presidential election if he is on the ballot as the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Imo West Senatorial District. Okorocha is locked in a legal battle with his successor, Governor Hope Uzodimma, over the APC ticket for Imo West, with both laying claim to victory in the party’s primary election. ﻿ The APC, however, submitted Uzodimma’s name to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as its candidate, prompting Okorocha to challenge the decision in court. On Thursday, the Federal Capital Territory High Court ruled that Okorocha secured the majority of votes cast in the primary and should be declared the winner. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today hours after the judgment, Okorocha said his presence on the ballot would guarantee Tinubu’s victory in the state. “What is important to me now is how Asiwaju will be elected in Imo State. With this, my name coming on the ballot paper now, Asiwaju can be sure that his victory is given in Imo State,” he said. The former governor celebrated the ruling, insisting that the judiciary was not for sale. He also said Uzodimma had “met his Waterloo,” alleging that the court had pronounced that his documents “were forged”. Okorocha urged people in the South-East to approach the 2027 presidential election strategically, advising the Igbo to put political calculations ahead of emotions. According to him, supporting Tinubu would amount to a strategic alliance that could benefit the South-East politically in the future. “As Southeasterners, we are not going to politics now with emotions; we have to go to politics with strategy. So, supporting Tinubu for Ndigbo is a strategic alliance,” he said. “We cannot afford to gamble for four years. Any time Nigerians think it is the time for Ndigbo to be president, we should be proper presidents.” Okorocha added that he would work more effectively with other South-East governors to secure Tinubu’s victory in the region if he were placed in charge of the president’s campaign in Imo State.
